# Cave slowness, second read: ceremony and throughput, not reasoning depth - 2026-10-04

**Skill:** Ecgberht (Cave of Wonders conversation, Aladdin); correction and extension of journal 2069 after John: "I don't see why the ultra high model with high effort generates so much dialogue and takes so long for such simple issues... I think that something else is going on."
**Input:** The same Codex thread (`rollout-2026-10-03T07-22-59-01a101ee-a39b-...jsonl`), the 51-minute turn at 2026-10-04T20:51Z step by step (each tool call, the wait before it, token usage per step); every Codex thread from 2026-10-02..04 compared by working directory.
**Work:** Classified the 56 tool calls of the 51-minute turn; summed per-step token usage; computed per-thread median turn length and seconds per step.
**Output:** About 5 of 56 calls changed Anchor code (high-seat-page.js x3, cockpit-feedback.js, app.js). The rest was ceremony: 7 rewrites of `.ecgberht/attention.json`, a new PLAN-v4.html, six new one-off scripts (verify-feedback.py, verify-feedback-delivery.py, record-feedback-refinement/checked/top.mjs, use-shared-feedback.py), make-feedback-report.py, DELIVERABLES reads, AGENTS.md re-reads, a sub-agent check. Token use for the turn: 7.73M input (7.41M cached, median 135k per step), 73k output, 36.5k reasoning (median 414 per step). All other cockpits run the same model and effort (gpt-6.1-sol / ultra): median working turn 5.6-15 min, 29-110 s per step (MIT Lectures 110 s); the Cave's 14.9 min median is typical, not an outlier.
**Result:** Journal 2069's emphasis was wrong in one respect: the time is not deep reasoning. Reasoning per step is small; each step still costs about 50 s, and generation ran at about 24 output tokens per second while a 135k-token context was resent every step. Two causes dominate: (1) the cockpit discipline (plan page, receipts, bespoke verification scripts, report, deliverable rows, attention writes) is applied in full to a small UI fix, multiplying steps by about ten; (2) per-step latency of this model tier on a large resent context. Effort level is a minor factor; lowering it would cut little and John does not want it lowered for hard problems.
**Friction:** None in the diagnosis. The status card's "Tests/Journal/ETA unavailable" during the turn gave John no way to see that the time was going to ceremony.
**Next:** Fix, in order of payoff: (a) size the ceremony to the change - a small reversible UI fix gets the edit, one check and a one-line receipt; the plan page, bespoke verifier and report only for real efforts (the LITE band rule already in AGENTS.md, which this conversation is not applying); (b) the steward hands real work to commissioned agents (coder, reviewer, swarms at the best model and full effort) and stays responsive, with an immediate receipt for a message sent mid-turn (John approved hand-off and receipts, 2026-10-04); (c) keep the steward's own thread small (a fresh thread seeded from the conversation log past about 150k tokens) so each of its steps resends less. Through an Ecgberht improvement cycle. Host Claude Code (Opus 5.5), read-only diagnosis, cross_model false.
